_doc: jStack systems registry — every system bundled by the jStack plugin (hooks, skills, runtime mechanisms) that must be tracked, documented, and live-testable. A host machine may federate this file into its own systems registry via an `imports:` field and stamps each entry with `origin: "jstack"` + the resolved plugin version at read time. Maintenance rule: every entry lives where its code lives — edit jStack systems in jStack, host systems in the host registry, never both. Every entry MUST declare a `test` so verification is callable on demand from any surface (CLI, dashboard, work-Claude debugging).

_schema.kind: hook | skill | system | subsystem — 'hook' = Claude Code lifecycle hook (PreToolUse, SessionStart, etc.). 'skill' = invocable slash-command skill shipped under skills/. 'system' = composite mechanism (rules-injection pipeline, install flow). 'subsystem' = nested sub-feature inside a parent.
_schema.name: string — display name
_schema.code: array of code paths (relative to plugin root)
_schema.config: array of config paths (relative to plugin root unless ~/-prefixed)
_schema.docs: array of doc paths inside the plugin

test.type: script | endpoint — 'script' = CLI executable, runs in-place, exit 0 = pass. 'endpoint' = HTTP POST handled by a host process (reserved for host-side wrappers).
test.path: string — for type=script, path relative to plugin root. for type=endpoint, URL path.
test.description: string — one-line description of what the test verifies

systems.name: Cross-Tree Rule Injection
systems.description: PreToolUse hook that injects path-matched ~/.claude/rules/*.md bodies into Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit calls — works regardless of session launch CWD, so cross-tree agents pick up the right conventions on every file mutation.

test.description: Live test of the real hook script via its PreToolUse JSON stdin contract: cold-fire (matches rule + emits additionalContext on first call), consecutive-dedup (same session, no transcript growth → no re-inject), threshold re-fire (transcript grown past JSTACK_RULE_REINJECT_BYTES → re-inject). Runs hermetically against a temp fixture via JSTACK_RULES_DIR + JSTACK_CACHE_ROOT overrides — never touches real markers or shipped rules.

systems.notes: Registered in hooks/hooks.json — Claude Code auto-loads when the plugin is installed. Kill switch: JSTACK_PATH_RULES_DISABLED=1. Re-fire threshold: JSTACK_RULE_REINJECT_BYTES (default 400000 ≈ 100K tokens). Defensive: any exception → silent exit 0, never blocks the tool. Marker files live at /tmp/jstack-rule-cache/<session_id>/<rule>.marker storing the transcript byte offset at last injection.

systems.name: Transcript Dialogue Read
systems.description: PreToolUse hook on Read that answers a session transcript — Claude session file or Codex rollout — with speech only: what the user said and what the agent said, with tool calls, tool results, reasoning, snapshots and injected wrappers stripped. A session .jsonl is an append-only machine log in which speech is a rounding error (355KB renders to 4KB), so reading one whole spends a context window on text nobody said. This was a rule in rules-stage and was routinely ignored, because reading a handed-over path is the obvious move; the reader changed instead of the instruction. Deliberate raw access via jq or grep is untouched, and every failure path falls through to the real read.

test.description: Pipes fixture PreToolUse payloads through the real hook against a temp tree. Asserts passthrough for ordinary files, non-Read tools and unrelated .jsonl; denial carrying both sides' speech for a Claude session file and a Codex rollout; that no tool call, tool result, thinking, meta, sidechain, snapshot or injected text survives either engine; that a <system-reminder> wrapped inside a real prompt is stripped without taking the prompt with it; and that an unparseable transcript falls through to the real read.

systems.name: SessionStart Timeline Injection
systems.description: SessionStart hook that injects the seat's last N timeline entries (via bin/log_event tail) into every new session as additionalContext — the READ half of the running-memory loop (the WRITE half is the session-end self-write / Stop-hook line). Which seats get injected and how many entries is the timeline_inject map in the review config ({"agent/submode": N, "*/submode": N}); unlisted seats get nothing. Sub-mode resolves from cwd: first segment under {agent_root}/{Name}, else 'chat' (cockpit sessions stay at the agent root, so the project-dir key / memory is never moved); 'review' is skipped. Liveness counts an IDE ancestor as well as a controlling terminal (JSTACK_IDE_ANCESTORS, default Xcode): an editor drives its embedded agent from a window, so no process in that chain holds a tty and a human would otherwise read as a headless spawn.

test.description: Live test of the real hook via its SessionStart JSON stdin contract against a hermetic temp agents tree (JSTACK_REVIEW_CONFIG override): agent-root cwd → 'chat' seat injected; explicit submode cwd → that seat's entries; 'review' submode → no output; non-workspace cwd → no-op; unlisted seat → nothing; interactive_only honored (headless spawn gets nothing, pty session injected); kill switch honored; emitted payload is valid SessionStart hook JSON.

systems.notes: Registered in hooks/hooks.json — auto-loads when the plugin is installed. Kill switch: JSTACK_TIMELINE_INJECT_DISABLED=1 (legacy JSTACK_CONTINUITY_INJECT_DISABLED honored). Reads agent_root + timeline_inject from JSTACK_REVIEW_CONFIG (default ~/.claude/jstack/review.json), same as the engine. Defensive: any error → exit 0, never blocks a session. Sub-mode resolution is kept identical to bin/session-review-spawn resolve_submode and the Stop hook's agent_source — if they drift, a seat reads back entries it never wrote.

systems.name: Install Rules
systems.description: Symlinks (or copies, with --copy) both user-scope stages a plugin cannot ship itself: rules-stage/ into ~/.claude/rules/ so bodies auto-load by glob match, and commands-stage/ into ~/.claude/commands/ so bare slash commands exist unnamespaced.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory.

systems.notes: Default mode symlinks, --copy snapshots for offline edit, --force overwrites. Links point at the checkout rather than the versioned cache path, which is reaped on update. /jstack:install-rules.

systems.name: Work
systems.description: Gets the agent battle-ready on a topic before doing the work: orient (date + injected seat timeline), resolve project → repo, determine stack, load every relevant skill via the Skill tool, survey recent changes (git log/status + topic file search), read the core files, and report a grounded lay of the land. Preparation only — no code changes, no state writes, no PR.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory.

systems.notes: Args: [@project] <topic>. No registry read — leans on the agent's own loaded identity for project + stack. @project resolves a repo name case-insensitively under userConfig.repo_root (default parent of agent_root); unknown → list candidates and stop. No @project → own project; multi-project agent + ambiguous topic → infer from topic, else ask one question. Skill selection matches stack+topic against live skill descriptions (no hardcoded table), loads inclusive. /jstack:work.

systems.name: Handoff
systems.description: Generates a concise session handoff doc and opens a fresh Claude Code terminal preloaded with it via bin/open-terminal-here. Supports @agent targeting: resolves another agent's workspace under user_config.agent_root and boots the new session there — walk-up does the identity switch.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/open-terminal-here adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [@agent] [focus]. @agent resolves {Name} case-insensitively under agent_root; target cwd = chat/ subdir if present else agent root; unknown name → list available agents and stop. Focus narrows scope. Writes handoff-context.md to the TARGET cwd, then open-terminal-here with --append-system-prompt-file. Cross-agent docs are briefings: name who hands off, mark user-locked decisions. Adapter overridable earlier in PATH. /jstack:handoff.

systems.name: Audit
systems.description: Writes a claims document (audit-brief.md: protocol + Original Issue / What Was Done / Claimed Verifications / Caution Flags / Blast Radius / Pitfalls) and opens a fresh terminal via bin/open-terminal-here where a trust-nothing auditor verifies every claim from source and reports CONFIRMED/REFUTED/UNVERIFIABLE. Report-only — the auditor changes nothing.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/open-terminal-here adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [focus] [@agent], order-agnostic. @agent resolves like handoff under agent_root (auditor boots under that agent's identity). Caution Flags section is mandatory — user-stated 'don't break X' constraints verbatim, verified first. Auto-start: kickoff prompt passed as a pre-quoted positional claude arg (adapter flattens args via $*). Auditor asks first only if genuinely blocked, else begins immediately. /jstack:audit.

systems.name: Recall
systems.description: Replays the timeline for a date or period and outlines what happened, scoped to an agent/submode or all seats. Reads through bin/log_event — the store is the only source, never a summary of it.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/log_event adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [yesterday|monday|jan 24|YYYY-MM-DD[..YYYY-MM-DD]] [agent[/submode]|all] [detailed]. Date-or-period questions only — a keyword question ("when did we ship X?") is a log_event grep, not this. /jstack:recall.

systems.name: Tag
systems.description: Files a session under a timeline subject. Typed by the user, `/tag` never reaches the model: hooks/tag-command.py answers it at UserPromptSubmit and blocks the prompt, so listing, attaching, minting and detaching all cost zero turns. The SKILL.md remains for the model tagging a session mid-turn in light of the work it has been doing.

test.description: Pipes fixture UserPromptSubmit payloads through the real hook against a temp JSTACK_TIMELINE_DIR; asserts every branch's text AND its exit code, since an answer on exit 0 has spent the turn the hook exists to save.

systems.notes: Grammar is one tag per call: bare lists the vocabulary with a marker on what the session carries; a carried name toggles off; a known name attaches; an unknown name needs trailing words to mint with, and is refused without them. Recognized as /tag, /jstack:tag, and the JSTACK_TAG_CMD sentinel the installed stub expands to, so it works whichever way the harness routes a command. The gates live in the CLI, not the caller.

systems.name: Pict
systems.description: Renders everything a session spawned from a directory is injected with, in wire order, and puts it on screen. Typed by the user, `/pict` never reaches the model: hooks/pict-command.py answers it at UserPromptSubmit and blocks the prompt. Render, place, open — three fixed steps, none of them a judgement, and a session asked to describe its own context describes what it believes is there, which is the guess the tool exists to replace.

test.description: Pipes fixture UserPromptSubmit payloads through the real hook against a temp tree with a faked renderer and faked openers; asserts placement, view selection, opener precedence and every failure branch's exit code — an answer on exit 0 has spent the turn the hook exists to save.

systems.notes: Bare is the default: the injection itself, no weights and no on-demand layer, because rules that fire when a file is touched are not what a session opens with. `--full` is the hook's own flag and drops --bare rather than forwarding one; a leading directory argument renders that instead of the session's cwd, and everything after it goes to pict untouched. The render lands in the workspace's pad when there is one, else CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/jstack/pict, under a name stable per directory so a second ask refreshes one document. Opening delegates to show-doc where the host has one (it knows which screen drives the session), open-artifact otherwise; with neither, the file is still written and its path is the answer. The SKILL.md carries no work the hook does not do; it exists so pict is reachable as /jstack:pict on a plain plugin install — the bare /pict stub only lands once /jstack:install-rules has run — and as the by-hand fallback for a harness that does not fire UserPromptSubmit on commands.

systems.name: Split Off
systems.description: Dubs the current session into a new terminal via bin/dub-session — a verbatim copy of the conversation under a fresh id, opened in its own window and diverging forward. Typed by the user, `/splitoff` never reaches the model: hooks/splitoff-command.py answers it at UserPromptSubmit and blocks the prompt. Where handoff distills to a brief, this keeps the whole transcript.

test.description: Pipes fixture UserPromptSubmit payloads through the real hook and the real dubber against a temp project tree with a faked terminal adapter; asserts the copy is a new id, the source is byte-identical after it, --resume is used and --session-id never, and that a refusal dubs nothing.

systems.notes: Words are the copy's NAME, appended to the source title so the resume picker tells two forks apart — never a scope, since splitoff dubs the whole transcript and never narrows (/jstack:handoff is the scoped restart). Blocking at UserPromptSubmit also cuts at the last completed turn, so the branch does not carry the turn that made it. The fork is built from the payload's transcript_path, not reconstructed from id + cwd. A terminal that will not open is a missing convenience, not a lost fork: the id and the resume line go out either way. Recognized as /splitoff, /jstack:splitoff, and the JSTACK_SPLITOFF_CMD sentinel.

systems.name: Takeover
systems.description: Spawns a fresh session — here or in another agent's workspace — pointed at THIS session's transcript and told to take it over. It is handed no summary: it reads the JSONL from source, checks the claims against the tree, and continues. Typed by the user, `/takeover` never reaches the model: hooks/takeover-command.py answers it at UserPromptSubmit and blocks the prompt. Where handoff distills the session to a brief it wrote itself and splitoff dubs it whole, this one hands over a pointer and a mandate to verify.

test.description: Pipes fixture UserPromptSubmit payloads through the real hook against a temp agent tree with a faked terminal adapter; asserts the briefing is a pointer and a mandate rather than a summary, that its user-spine recipe selects queue-operation/enqueue so mid-turn corrections are not invisible, that --first-prompt is detected rather than assumed and its absence said out loud, that @agent/@agent-seat resolve through the shared grammar, that the slash form this command shipped with for one release is corrected rather than reported as a bad agent, and that an unknown one spawns nothing, and that a missing transcript or a dead window reports a failure instead of a spawn.

systems.notes: Args: [@agent[-seat]] [focus]. Target cwd comes from root.resolve_seat, the one address grammar shared with mail and the scheduler — deterministic, because a hook has no judgement to apply; handoff's focus-aware sub-mode pick is a model's call and is not available here, so the report names the directory it chose. The spawned name is `TO · <current source session title>` (or `TO→Agent · ...` when retargeted); focus narrows only the briefing and kickoff, never the title. Claude titles come from the transcript's latest custom/generated title and Codex titles from the last matching session_index row; an unnamed source falls back to its seat. Two channels into the spawn and both are load-bearing: --prompt-file is the standing mandate (appended system prompt, survives compaction), --first-prompt is the provider's positional argument and is what makes the spawn a TASK rather than a staged context. --first-prompt is newer than --prompt-file and the adapter is overridable by design, so support is probed (`open-terminal-here` with no args prints its usage) — an adapter that does not parse it would pass it to the provider, which dies on an unknown option. The briefing's user-spine jq selects queue-operation/enqueue alongside user: a message typed while a turn was running is not filed as a user record, and those interjections are usually the corrections. Recognized as /takeover, /jstack:takeover, and the JSTACK_TAKEOVER_CMD sentinel.

systems.name: Print Transcript Path
systems.description: Prints the absolute path of the session's local JSONL transcript file — the answer to "where is this conversation stored on disk". Typed by the user, `/print` never reaches the model: hooks/print-command.py answers it at UserPromptSubmit from the payload's own transcript_path and blocks the prompt.

test.description: Pipes fixture UserPromptSubmit payloads through the real hook against a fixture CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; asserts the payload path is the answer verbatim, that the id glob never degrades to the newest file in a shared project dir, and every branch's exit code — an answer on exit 0 has spent the turn the hook exists to save.

systems.notes: No args; trailing words are ignored rather than refused. The harness hands every hook the file it is writing to, so the answer needs no glob and no path-encoding guess — the session-id glob remains only as the fallback for a payload without transcript_path, and never degrades to the newest .jsonl in the project dir, which is another session's conversation. Recognized as /print, /jstack:print, and the JSTACK_PRINT_CMD sentinel the installed stub expands to. The SKILL.md is the by-hand fallback for a harness that does not fire UserPromptSubmit on commands.

systems.name: Prompt Injection Check (pict)
systems.description: bin/pict renders everything a session spawned from a given directory would actually receive — globals, CLAUDE.md walk-up, auto-memory, timeline injection, anchored path rules, hook injectors — as one ordered markdown document with per-source token weights. The way to see a seat's real context budget instead of reasoning about it. Two views: the default answers why each file is in the context and what it costs; --bare answers what the context IS — the injected bodies in wire order, no weights, no notes, no on-demand layer.

test.description: Hermetic run against a fixture home tree, fixture rules, fixture review config and a stub log_event — no real ~/.claude or timeline touched.

systems.notes: Answers "what does this seat actually load" from the real injectors rather than from what the mds claim. Resolves symlinks (macOS /var → /private/var) when keying a directory.

systems.name: Timeline Log
systems.description: Timeline sqlite store ({timeline_dir}/timeline.db) written and read by bin/log_event — block format, chronological order, pipeline-task consolidation, direct/indirect origin, and a session→tag relation naming the subject a stretch of work was about. The day's spine: feeds daily briefs, nightly reviews, and seat injection.

test.description: Runs the real bin/log_event against a temp JSTACK_TIMELINE_DIR: block format, detail bullets, chronological insertion, blank-line separation, pipeline-task consolidation (one live block, earliest ts), headline collapse, bad-arg rejection. Tags: the relation migrates onto a pre-tag db, `tag new` needs a description, `tag set` refuses an unknown name instead of minting it, --tag on tail/grep/recall resolves entries through session_id, an undefined tag errors rather than returning silence, and a write with no --session inherits CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while the explicit flag still wins.

subsystems.name: Stop Timeline Reminder
subsystems.description: Stop hook that blocks an auto session's first stop once, with a log_event reminder, so a cron-spawned run cannot end without writing its timeline entry. A marker makes the second stop pass through, so it reminds rather than loops.

test.description: Pipes fixture Stop-hook JSON through the real hook: auto session blocks once then passes, stop_hook_active honored, user-engaged and tiny transcripts never block, SKIP_SESSION_HOOK=1 never blocks.

subsystems.notes: Only auto sessions are in scope — a typed/TUI transcript is never blocked, since a human ending a session is not a session skipping its record.

systems.notes: Self-contained python3 stdlib — no venv, no host imports. Timeline dir override: JSTACK_TIMELINE_DIR (default ~/Logs/Timeline). Format spec is the rules-stage/timeline.md rule (install via /jstack:install-rules). Hosts with an in-process timeline writer must keep format parity — pin it with a host-side parity test against this bin.

systems.name: Session-End Engine
systems.description: SessionEnd hook → bin/session-review-spawn engine → session_end_action. Default 'selfwrite': resume a disposable DUB of the just-ended session (bin/dub-session) for ONE turn to write its own seat-tagged timeline entry and pick the session's subject tag from the shared vocabulary, then delete the dub — the primary transcript never grows a self-write turn (clean future resume, clean picker; stale dubs pid-swept every engine run). A resumed session that ends again gets the engine-computed last-reviewed boundary injected, scoping the entry to the delta since the resume point. A COMPACTED session gets a second injected note: a compact starts a new root, so the resumed dub holds a summary of the earlier turns rather than the turns, and the note names the loss, lifts the prompt's no-re-read rule for the session's own transcript alone, and hands over the jq for the user prose (log line carries 'compacted xN'). Legacy 'review': claude --print from {agent_root}/{Name}/review/ running the review skill → output parser-validated → retry → escalate (thread extraction + doc reconciliation). Keeps the timeline truthful after every session.

test.description: Imports the real engine under a hermetic temp config: output validator (good passes; missing section / evidence-free walk / log_event-claimed-but-timeline-didn't-grow reject; 'no user turns' + cron paraphrases accepted; host-extended section lists enforced), agent resolution (umbrella dirs, project_dir_map, $HOME → default_agent, review/-dir reviewable convention), atomic claim dedup (live pid loses, stale pid taken over), SPAWN log-line dashboard contract, and the selfwrite prompt itself (formats with every placeholder, names the seat source, links and tags the ORIGINAL session, reads the tag vocabulary before writing to it, steps numbered once each, host-only stamp step omitted where the tool doesn't exist, resume-delta boundary injected only when there is one). Compaction: compact_scope counts only real compact_boundary lines, dates the last, ignores boundaries before the reviewed offset, and claims nothing on an unreadable transcript; the injected note names the count and time, points at the session's own transcript, lifts the no-re-read rule and carries a runnable jq, and is absent entirely when the session never compacted.

systems.notes: session_end_action selects the behavior: 'selfwrite' (default) resumes the ended session (bin/log_event on the spawned PATH, selfwrite_model/selfwrite_max_turns/selfwrite_timeout_secs) and re-records the reviewed offset past the appended write so a reopen doesn't re-fire; 'review' runs the fresh review/ session (skill_invocation, required_sections, model, max_turns, timeout_secs, tg_classify_cmd, escalate_cmd); 'off' does nothing. Stack requirements: agent workspaces under agent_root with {Name}/review/ (reviewable convention). Config: JSTACK_REVIEW_CONFIG (default ~/.claude/jstack/review.json) — agent_root, default_agent, project_dir_map, extra_path, log_file, plus the action-specific keys above. Kill switch: JSTACK_REVIEW_DISABLED=1. Loop guard: SKIP_SESSION_HOOK=1 on every spawn. Multi-entry-point safe: per-session atomic claim means a host SessionEnd hook and the plugin hook never double-act.

systems.name: Push
systems.description: Commits and pushes the work touched in the current session to whatever repo(s) those files live in — supports session-scoped (default) or all-pending (`all`) modes, and `0` to commit without pushing.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory.

subsystems.name: Session File List
subsystems.description: Prints the paths a session wrote, read from its own transcript — the stage list for /push, so which files are mine is never inferred from a shared working tree.

test.description: Drives the real binary against a fixture HOME, a synthetic transcript and a throwaway repo: the stage list is written-paths intersected with what git still sees a change at, in first-write order, deduped; subagent (sidechain) writes are included and Read/Bash calls are not; unchanged, gitignored and non-repo paths stay out of the stage list while remaining in --all and --json; a tracked file deleted on disk still stages; a torn final transcript line is skipped rather than fatal; a file another session left dirty is structurally unlistable. Every blind case — no session id, no transcript, one id matching two transcripts — exits nonzero instead of returning an empty list.

subsystems.notes: The list comes from the transcript and never from `git status` — that is what stops a dirty shared tree from being a judgment call, and why an agent can stage all of it without deciding anything. Blind spot by design: writes made through Bash (mv, sed -i, a script emitting files) never become tool calls, so /push still adds those by hand. Transcript resolution matches the print skill — id-globbed across project dirs, never newest-by-mtime, which under concurrent sessions hands back another session's file. Also answers for a dead session (--session <id>), which is how orphaned work gets attributed to whoever actually wrote it.

systems.notes: Authorization gate: only runs if the user explicitly said push/commit/ship/land in this session. Resolves repos from the touched-file list (works from a non-repo cockpit). Hard rules: no --no-verify, no --amend, no Co-Authored-By, no `git add -A`, sensitive paths skipped, never force-push main/master. `all` mode groups pending changes into per-unit-of-work commits with a one-line plan up front. /jstack:push.

systems.name: Report
systems.description: Closes out a task: every finding is settled as its own commit or a filed GitHub issue before the report is written, so nothing real leaves the session as prose.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory, and the file-issue adapter it calls is present and executable.

subsystems.name: Issue Filing
subsystems.description: Files a GitHub issue for an unfixed finding AND places it on the board its owner reads, resolving repo -> project -> intake column live from GitHub. Exactly one type label (bug / optimization / feature) is required and created on repos that lack it.

test.description: Drives the real binary against a stub gh: a filed issue is added to its board and the intake column set (TODO/Backlog/Triage found by name, never by position); a repo linked to no project still files, one linked to several is skipped rather than guessed unless --project names it; a project marked [not-intake] is excluded so a work board cannot steal filing, though --project still selects it; exactly one type label is required and a missing one is created on the repo, with an uncreatable one filing untyped and saying type=none in its receipt; an unknown non-type label is dropped instead of taking the issue down; and every blind or refusing state - no gh, failed graphql, null repo, issues disabled, no body - exits nonzero so the caller can never report a number it did not get.

subsystems.notes: Board routing is read live from repository.projectsV2 rather than a local repo->board map, because a second copy of a fact GitHub already owns rots silently. Placement is best-effort AFTER creation: an issue that files but fails to board still exits 0 with board=none in its receipt, since losing the issue would be the worse outcome. Portable with no config: a machine whose repos are linked to no project gets plain issues.

systems.notes: Fixed, or filed - the rule the skill enforces. A break in reach gets fixed and becomes its own commit; a break not fixed becomes an issue in the owning repo, with a body a cold reader can act on. Replaces the reporting template that used to live in the host root CLAUDE.md, where findings could be mentioned in prose and lost at session end. Commit mechanics are NOT restated here - the skill hands committing to /jstack:push, which owns the commit contract. /jstack:report.

systems.name: Elevator
systems.description: Delivers a finished unit of work spoken aloud in three or four short blocks - where it stands, what it took, what is next - with no paths, symbol names, shas, issue numbers or counts in it. Carries report's settling obligation: unsettled work is fixed-or-filed and pushed before it is spoken.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, and name matches directory.

systems.notes: Report's obligations, a person's mouth. Same gate as /jstack:report (settle every finding, then /jstack:push) with a different delivery: four to six sentences broken across a block per beat, blank line between, no headers or bullets, nothing a listener would have to open. A single unbroken wall is the failure the form exists to end, however short. Blocked/unverified work takes its own block rather than being folded away - compression buys no silence. Optional arg is a focus that narrows which aspect the paragraph answers; a focus on untouched work is declined in one line rather than inferred. Reachable unnamespaced as /elevator via commands-stage, installed by /jstack:install-rules. /jstack:elevator.

systems.name: Issue
systems.description: Works one assigned GitHub issue from open to a PR: reads the brief, builds the fix in a worktree, opens the PR, answers on the issue. Cards move process-side on the events the worker fires; the session never places one.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, and name matches directory.

subsystems.name: Board Placement
subsystems.description: Puts an existing issue on a work board and sets its status column. The board is named by configuration (board.project_id, else board.org) or by --project-id/--owner; its title and columns are read live from GitHub.

test.description: Drives the real binary against a stub gh: the card is added AND its column set, and a column that could not be set is reported as unset with exit 5 rather than claimed; an exact board title beats a substring that also matches, an ambiguous or unknown title exits 4 without placing, and a closed board is not a placement target; a user-owned account resolves like an org one even though gh exits non-zero on that call; the dry run mutates nothing and exits 5 on a column that does not exist. The config half asserts which account was searched and which board id was used rather than the receipt, because the stub answers the same boards to every owner: an out-of-org repo searches board.org and never the repo owner, board.project_id skips the owner search and survives a rename, --owner and a --board naming another board both send it back to a title search, and a stale or closed configured id exits 4 naming the id and the file it came from.

subsystems.notes: Companion to file-issue, and a different act: file-issue answers where a NEW finding goes (an intake column, by repo linkage); this answers where work-in-progress is visible (a work board, named by config). Adding is idempotent, so a re-fired event does not duplicate the card. Sessions never place their own cards - a host card engine shells to this binary on GitHub events. Which board is a property of the operation, not of the repo: one board tracks work across every repo, a Projects v2 board accepts items from any repo, and resolving it from the repo owner instead made every out-of-org repo unplaceable because a personal account has no board of its own. Only the board's identity is configured - a node id that does not change; its title and its columns are still read live for the same reason file-issue reads linkage live, because a local board->column table is a second copy of a fact GitHub owns.

subsystems.name: Worktree Interlock
subsystems.description: Takes the worktree for an issue, or refuses to work beside a session that already holds it. Tries the create form first and treats its failure as the signal that somebody has been here, then scans the live process table for an owner before calling it a resume.

test.description: Drives the real binary against real processes and real worktrees, not stubs - a stubbed process table would only prove a fixture parses. Fake sessions are made with exec -a so argv[0] really is claude and cwd is a real directory lsof can be asked about, and the fixture must use a two-command script because bash exec-optimizes a single one and the process silently stops resembling a session. A fresh issue creates the tree; a live owner is refused with its pid and start time and nothing is created; an owner with NO ref in argv but standing in the worktree is still refused, which is the --resume shape argv alone cannot see; a session does not refuse itself through its own ancestor; #420 does not match #42; a non-agent process carrying the ref is not an owner; a dead owner resumes with a receipt saying what was checked; and an unreadable process table refuses rather than reporting a clear machine.

subsystems.notes: The branch is issue-<N> and the worktree is {seat}/pad/issue-<N>, both derived from the number, so two dispatches on one issue land in one checkout by construction rather than by accident. The skill used to print both worktree commands and let the session pick between them, which spent the only available signal on a guess: the create form fails when the branch or path already exists, and a session reading that as a resume throws the detection away. Ownership is decided from what is running, never from a record - a registry row can outlive its process or be reaped out from under it. Two observables, either sufficient: the issue ref in argv, and cwd inside the worktree. The second is not redundant, because a session that adopted its issue from a comment on another issue carries no ref in argv at all. Identity is argv[0]'s basename, the same rule the host process scan uses, since 'claude' as a substring also matches unrelated tooling; the ref is matched with a digit boundary so #420 is not #42; and self plus every ancestor is excluded, without which every dispatch refuses itself and the skill can never run. Fails closed: an unreadable scan reports occupied, because a look that failed must not answer as a look that found nothing.

systems.name: Task
systems.description: Hands a unit of work to an agent as a GitHub task issue: the issue is the task, its comments are the conversation, its PR is the delivery, the merge is the close. Filing embeds the creating session in the body and assigns the executor account - the assignment is the spawn.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory, and the task-create adapter it calls is present and executable.

subsystems.name: Task Filing
subsystems.description: Files the issue through file-issue (which keeps type labels, board routing and every filing degradation), embeds the creator marker resolved through bin/msg's own session->seat logic, then assigns the executor account last so the loop the worker joins is fully formed.

test.description: Drives the real binary against a stubbed file-issue and gh in a fake HOME: the creator marker rides the filed body when the session resolves and its absence degrades to a loud marker-less filing, never a refusal; the executor is assigned on the filed number and a failed assignment exits 6 with assigned=none so filed-but-spawnless is never read as success; --no-assign files without touching gh; a file-issue refusal propagates untouched with nothing assigned; the dry run previews the assignment without making it; and a missing title or body refuses before anything happens.

subsystems.notes: The marker is the creator leg: the host webhook reads it from the issue body to deliver every later comment into the CLI that filed the task. Session->seat resolution is imported from bin/msg at run time rather than copied, so the one resolution logic cannot fork. Assignment is deliberately the last act and deliberately separable: --no-assign is the kill-switch and night-auditor path, where the issue waits fully formed for someone else to assign.

systems.name: Show Me
systems.description: Surfaces the result of the current topic in its real viewer instead of describing it. A fidelity-ladder command: mode token raw|live picks source-code vs live-running surface, default prefers an in-code preview. Classifies the artifact (code, preview, image, doc, mockup, data, app, web page, diff) and opens it via bin/open-artifact / Xcode (xed) / sim. Optional focus arg narrows which artifact.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/open-artifact adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [raw|live] [focus]. mode = reserved token on the fidelity ladder: raw -> source code (iOS: xed <View>.swift in Xcode; mockup/doc -> its .html/.svg/.md source not the render); default -> cheapest visual, prefers an in-code preview (SwiftUI #Preview in Xcode canvas, Storybook, Quick Look) over a heavier surface; live -> running env (sim build+launch+screenshot, dev server + live URL) via the project's run/sim/device skill. focus narrows the artifact; omitted shows the most recent salient result. Static artifacts (image/pdf): default==live==open in viewer, raw==source-if-any. Fallbacks: requested surface unavailable -> drop to nearest rung and say so; no visual -> textual render; adapter/xed nonzero -> report absolute path. bin/open-artifact self-detects platform (open / xdg-open|gio / start), overridable earlier in PATH. /jstack:showme.

systems.name: Day Audit
systems.description: Reverifies a whole day's shipped work across every repo, each audited under its OWNING agent for real domain context. Treats that day's timeline (the agents' claims) as a claims document, gathers the day's commits in each repo under repo_root (all refs), resolves each repo to its owning agent via the agent registry, fans out one regression auditor per repo-with-commits told to load that agent's role file + the repo's CLAUDE.md first (focus on bug-fix commits: real fix? regressed another issue? broke a consumer? smuggled in something big?), then synthesizes an IMPROVED/NEUTRAL/REGRESSED verdict per app and flags claim<->commit gaps. Report-only on code; always writes one timeline block recording the verdict.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory, bin/log_event is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [today|yesterday|<date>], date normalized in python3 (defaults today). Portable repo discovery: repo_root userConfig, else parent of agent_root, scanned for */.git. Ownership: agent_registry userConfig (else {agent_root}/agents.json) — each agent entry's {workspace, repos}; repo<->registry matched by normalized name (case + _/- folded) against BOTH local dir basename and git origin, so Acme_iOS==Acme-iOS. Owning-agent context delivered by instructing the auditor to read {workspace}/CLAUDE.md + {repo}/CLAUDE.md first (in-process subagents don't inherit a foreign CLAUDE.md via cwd); unowned repo -> generic auditor, coverage never drops. Per-day commits via `git log --all --no-merges --since/--until --date=local` so develop/feature/pushed work is covered. Verdict logged to the AUDITED day's file: `log_event day-audit --at <now> --date <DAY> --pipeline-task day-audit#<DAY>` — one block per day, replaced on re-run. Report-only on repos (never edits code); high-severity findings re-verified by the parent before repeating. /jstack:day-audit.

systems.name: Root Derivation
systems.description: The one declaration a jStack install derives its tree from. $JSTACK_ROOT (else a caller-supplied cfg 'root', else $HOME) yields Agents/, Systems/, Config/, State/, Logs/ and Credentials/ by structure — visible, declared folders, never a hidden dotfolder, because a hidden state dir is a second shadow root and that is the disease this cures. Each derived dir keeps its own env override above the derivation and a cfg key between them, so an install that names dirs explicitly is untouched by the derivation existing. Also the single definition of an agent — a directory under agents_dir() with a CLAUDE.md, or with a seat subdir carrying one — behind agents()/resolve_agent()/seats(), replacing copies that had drifted apart across the scheduler, both hooks, repo_seat and msg. Also the one seat-address grammar behind resolve_seat/seat_at/enclosing_seat and the `seat` CLI: an agent alone is its cockpit, hyphens walk down the seat tree, a seat holding its own chat/ resolves to that operator seat, and a pad is never a seat nor walked through to find one. The hyphen is structure here, which is why resolve_agent's separator fold is the wrong tool for an address — it reads work-ops and workops as one agent, so reached for by an addressing caller it answers None for every hyphenated seat id. A Seat derives all three spellings (the hyphen id, the timeline slash form, the directory) from one resolution, because hand-built at their use sites they drifted: a wake booked from alice/social/threads was labelled alice-social and booted one seat above the session that asked for it.

test.description: Hermetic tmpdir roots with HOME redirected: the six-dir derivation from JSTACK_ROOT; env > cfg > derivation precedence per dir, resolved per call so an env change mid-process takes effect; the legacy 'agent_root' cfg key installs already set; an explicit JSTACK_STATE_DIR outranking the derivation, which is the property that keeps a live daemon's state in place; a data dir inside the shipping checkout raising while agents_dir inside a repo stays legal; the agent taxonomy (top-level CLAUDE.md, seat-only, plain folder, dotdir) through agents/resolve_agent/seats including case and separator folding; the address grammar (cockpit descent, hyphen walking, a hyphenated agent name winning over agent+seat, pads refused, ids that round-trip, and enclosing_seat finding the seat a checkout sits under); and a bare-root proof asserting every answer comes from a tmpdir holding only Agents/alice/CLAUDE.md, never the machine's own tree.

systems.notes: Imports nothing from the package and reads no config file — callers pass their own parsed cfg, so there is one opinion about which file is authoritative. scheduler/config.py carries its own copy of the shipping-tree guard deliberately: it must keep working on an older install where root.py is absent, and importing the other way would be a cycle. Only Config/State/Logs/Credentials are guarded; Agents/ and Systems/ may legitimately live inside a repo. Resolution is never cached at import — a constant captured at import answers with the environment of a process start nobody remembers.

systems.name: Suite tree pin
systems.description: Makes jStack's own suite answer about the checkout it ships in. The pre-push gate runs the tests with JSTACK_PYTHON pointed at the host's venv (the scheduler suite needs dateutil), and that venv carries a .pth doing sys.path.insert(0, ~/jStack/plugins/jstack) so the host's daemon can find the plugin. Position 0 outranks PYTHONPATH, and every issue is worked in a worktree by mandate — so `import root` in a test resolved to the MAIN checkout: a false red on root.sh's shipping-tree guard, and a false green for any change to root.py, repo_seat.py or scheduler/* pushed from a worktree. tests/lib/pin-plugin-root.sh is sourced by every test that starts an interpreter touching plugin python; it fronts tests/lib on PYTHONPATH, where a sitecustomize imports jstack_pin — sitecustomize being the one hook imported after the last .pth — and then asserts the pin took, exiting the test if it did not.

test.description: Stages the defect in a tmpdir — a decoy plugin copy, a throwaway venv carrying the host venv's .pth line verbatim, and a stand-in tree being pushed — then proves: the hijack reproduces without the pin (a control, so a green below cannot mean the fixture never staged); the pinned tree wins the import; root.py's shipping-tree guard fires on the tree under test and names it (the false green, as behaviour); a module present only in the rival copy does not import; a pin that cannot take exits the test loudly instead of answering about another checkout; tests/root.sh passes end to end under the hijacking interpreter; and the .pth is left byte-identical and still wins for any interpreter outside the suite.

systems.notes: Two layers, because each alone loses to something. sys.path is reordered (this tree first, rival checkouts of the same plugin dropped by top-level signature) — that beats the .pth, since sitecustomize is imported after every .pth while PYTHONPATH is read before site runs. And a meta_path finder sits directly in front of PathFinder, because sys.path order is not final either: CPython prepends the script dir (or cwd, for -c) to sys.path[0] AFTER site has run, so a test invoked from inside another checkout gets it handed back at position 0. The finder declines submodules and loader-less directory hits, so tests/ and bin/ are never claimed as namespace packages. jstack_pin is self-locating — the tree it pins is the tree it ships in — so there is no env var to lose across an `env -i`. The .pth is not the defect and is not touched: the gate handing that interpreter to a hermetic suite is. Only the FIRST sitecustomize on the path is imported, so scheduler-bare.sh and schedule-self.sh (each installing one to block dateutil) import jstack_pin from their own shim and re-assert. manifest.sh gates both halves: `import root` must resolve under the plugin root, and any top-level test script that imports plugin python must source the helper.

systems.name: Doctor
systems.description: Install validator — one command that answers 'is this jStack working, and if not which part'. Thirteen checks over the same seams the tools read at runtime (root derivation, agent resolution, the spawn path, hooks.json, the rules/commands stages, the scheduler service), graded ok/warn/fail with the worst grade as the exit status. Read-only: it never creates the paths it reports on.

test.description: Proves the two properties a validator is believed on: that a full run against an empty sandbox root creates and removes nothing (the probe used to mkdir its own subject and then call it healthy), and that the exit status is the worst individual grade with the JSON agreeing. Plus the gradings that decide a fresh install's diagnosis — no agents is a failure, absent-but-creatable dirs are not, a dead rules symlink is a failure rather than an installed rule, an unparseable scheduler.json is a failure because both readers swallow it silently, and a check that raises surfaces as fail instead of vanishing from the list.

systems.notes: `jstack-doctor` for the table, `jstack-doctor --json` for a harness. Exit 0 ok / 1 warn / 2 fail. Run it before anything else when diagnosing an install, and after any scheduler install. Stdlib-only; imports `root` and `scheduler.config`/`scheduler.spawn` out of the plugin root so every answer comes from the module that owns it.

systems.name: Scheduler
systems.description: Deterministic daemon that fires one-time and recurring agent runs on RFC-5545 RRULE schedules — the piece that lets jStack START a session, not just review and remember one. Timeout counts from spawn, the daemon owns child pgids, TTFT/stall watchdogs kill hung turns, catch-up covers downtime.

test.description: Runs the real package against a hermetic temp SCHEDULER_HOME: install config drives timezone/spawn env/spawn PATH; workspace resolution (override > resolver hook > registry > agent_root) with seat_rules applied only when the seat is real; a broken resolver spec raises rather than silently relocating every run; permission_mode defaults to bypassPermissions and resolves job>category>default; a printed job time labelled with the zone abbreviation of that instant rather than of now, asserted on both sides of the DST transition; VTIMEZONE derived for US-DST, last-Sunday and no-DST zones; registry add/list/remove round-trip through the CLI; and a real daemon boot serving /health. Skips with a clear message when the host python lacks python-dateutil. Never touches a real registry, state dir, or running daemon.

subsystems.name: Scheduler — bare install
subsystems.description: The guarantee that a fresh install can schedule before it has installed anything. python-dateutil is the package's only third-party dependency and only recurring jobs need it; one-shot jobs are how a message wake and a self-scheduled follow-up are delivered, so they must book on a stock interpreter. Held by a lazy accessor (occurrences.get_rrulestr) that both call sites and the registry validator go through.

test.description: Blocks dateutil via a sitecustomize meta_path finder regardless of what the host interpreter has — so the guarantee is proved on machines that DO have the package, not only where it was already fine. Asserts the blocker took effect before trusting any later check, then: scheduler.cli imports, add-once books, the job is really in the registry, and a recurring job fails naming python-dateutil rather than surfacing an ImportError as a bad-rrule error.

subsystems.notes: Regression guarded: occurrences.py imported rrulestr at module top and cli.py imports occurrences, so on any python without dateutil the CLI died at import and add-once never reached argparse — which on a second machine read as 'the tools do not work here'. The registry validator separately wrapped its own import in the rrule try/except, reporting a missing package as a malformed schedule string; it now resolves the accessor outside that try.

subsystems.name: Scheduler — self-booked wakes
subsystems.description: The self-wake primitive: an agent's 'I'll check back at three' becomes a real one-shot or a loud non-zero exit, never a silent nothing. bin/schedule-self infers agent and seat from cwd through root.py, reads times in the scheduler's configured timezone rather than a hardcoded region, refuses a time already past, pins the seat as the job's workspace, and books through `scheduler.cli add-once` — the same subprocess path the inbox wake uses, so there is one way to book a job. --resume fork-resumes the calling conversation: session id from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, workspace pinned to the directory the session started in because that string is what names the transcript's project slug. An omitted timeout ships no per-job value so the category's runway governs; pinning the global default at the call site would silently override the category and kill a legitimately-long wake mid-flight.

test.description: Hermetic bare root (only Agents/alice/chat/CLAUDE.md), tmpdir SCHEDULER_HOME, and the scheduler-bare dateutil blocker so the stock-interpreter guarantee is proved on machines that have the package. Asserts by reading the registry back, never by trusting exit 0: agent, workspace, message and configured tz on a real booking; the seat pinned from a subdirectory; agent-dir resolution with no seat; outside-tree and past-time refusals booking nothing; --resume pinning cwd and carrying the session id, and failing without the env var, from the wrong dir, or with no transcript; an explicit timeout reaching the job while an omitted one leaves no per-job value; below-runway timeouts refused; category pass-through; and name-based idempotency so a repeated booking cannot double-fire.

subsystems.notes: Booking env matches bin/msg's _sched_argv with one deliberate inversion: an explicit SCHEDULER_HOME env outranks mail.scheduler_home, per the root model's rule that explicit env is the top rung. The port dropped the origin machine's message-prefix category inference, its social-slot plumbing and its host-policy timeout ceiling — those are one operation's settings, not the tool's. The timeout test asserts the value is None rather than the key's absence: cli._base_job writes an omitted flag as an explicit null and resolve._present reads null and absent as the same fact.

subsystems.name: Scheduler — service install
subsystems.description: The missing half of a fresh install: booking works everywhere, firing only works where a daemon runs, so the default experience of a second machine was 'I scheduled it and nothing happened' — the most confusing failure the system can produce. The daemon has two shapes and the machine decides which. Where jStack Hub is installed it is one of the HUB's own sealed services (live.jstack.hub.scheduler, plist inside the bundle, registered by the signed app through SMAppService, run by JStackRuntime) — so bin/jstack-scheduler REFUSES install there and its status/restart/logs/uninstall act on that service; macOS groups background items by the registering app, so all of jStack is one Login Items row instead of one row per daemon, and one plist means one claim on the daemon's port. Without a Hub bin/jstack-scheduler turns `python3 -m scheduler` into a supervised per-user service it owns (launchd LaunchAgent on macOS, systemd user unit on Linux) generated from the same resolution the daemon boots with: the resolved root frozen into the definition because launchd strips the environment, explicit SCHEDULER_*/JSTACK_* overrides passed through, spawn_dirs expanded into the service PATH so a stripped environment cannot lose `claude`, and stdout/stderr under root.state_dir() — never the checkout. Idempotent install, ownership-stamped files it refuses to overwrite when it did not write them, --dry-run on install and uninstall, and a status that probes definition, process and API separately rather than reporting one and implying the others.

test.description: Never loads, unloads or writes a real service: HOME is redirected into a tmpdir and every invocation is --dry-run or status. Parses the emitted plist with plistlib rather than grepping it (validity, RunAtLoad/KeepAlive, -m scheduler, the root in env, logs under that root's State, no data path inside the checkout); asserts the default label differs from the label the origin machine's own daemon runs under; that dry-run writes no file, creates no directory and loads nothing; that a hand-rolled definition is refused and left untouched; that a missing python-dateutil is named as a warning rather than a refusal; that an unsupported platform exits non-zero with a runnable foreground command; and that status on an absent label reports not-installed and exits 3 without raising.

subsystems.notes: com.jstack.scheduler is the label of the STANDALONE service only — the Hub's is live.jstack.hub.scheduler, and the two must never collide or uninstalling one would unload the other. It is namespaced under the product rather than an operator's reverse-domain so a file carrying it can only be a file this tool wrote. A surviving com.jstack.scheduler.plist on a Hub machine is a jstack-doctor FAIL, not a warning: two rows and two processes racing one port, which nothing self-corrects. JSTACK_SCHEDULER_HUB moves the Hub's location so the refusal and the Hub-mode verbs are provable on a machine without one. JSTACK_SCHEDULER_PLATFORM overrides sys.platform so the unsupported path is testable on a supported machine. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 refused or unhealthy, 2 unsupported or usage, 3 status-not-installed. verify/scenarios/plugin/scheduler.sh drives a real install and launchctl load on a Hub-less guest; verify/scenarios/hub/install.sh proves the Hub-owned shape by reading each job's parent bundle identifier.

systems.notes: One package, every machine — nothing about a host is written into it. A host declares itself in {install}/config/scheduler.json: timezone, spawn_env, spawn_path_prepend, spawn_dirs, workspace_resolver ('module:function') + python_path, agent_root / agent_registry, seat_rules. SCHEDULER_HOME roots config/ and state/ (default: the package's parent); SCHEDULER_CONFIG_DIR / STATE_DIR / CREDENTIALS_DIR / API_PORT / INSTALL_FILE override individually. Requires python-dateutil and the claude CLI. Runs under launchd/systemd as `python3 -m scheduler`; mutations go through `python3 -m scheduler.cli`. permission_mode defaults to bypassPermissions because an unattended run has nobody to answer a prompt — narrowing it per job or per category is deliberate, not a default to reach for. Control API binds 127.0.0.1 only, no auth.

systems.name: Agent Inbox
systems.description: Addressed messaging in two forms — an UPDATE to a seat, delivered once at its next SessionStart; a TASK to a session, which spawns one, ties it to the sender's, and opens a two-way channel enforced at Stop. bin/msg writes a `messages` table alongside the timeline and is its only sanctioned writer.

test.description: Runs the real bin/msg against a temp timeline dir, temp agent tree and its own HOME: seat addressing (cockpit descent, hyphenated seat dirs, @self), refusal of non-seat dirs / unknown agents / @boss, send-read-reply-thread roundtrip, attachments copied into the receiver's pad (and recorded in place when already there), a task that cannot be delivered filing nothing at all, and THE CHANNEL — the sender's session on the row with no receiver until one claims it, the stamp a woken run leaves, the reply binding to the session that asked rather than to its seat, the resume wake booked against that session's own workspace, delivery consuming the answer and cancelling the wake it beat, a runaway channel that stops waking anyone, one timeline entry per seat at close, and a printed wake time labelled with the zone abbreviation of that instant rather than of now, asserted on both sides of the DST transition.

subsystems.name: Inbox Stop Guard
subsystems.description: Serves both ends of a channel, once per (session, message) — blocks a session that owes an answer, and hands a session the answer it asked for. Binds only what is addressed to that exact session: the [inbox:N] its own first prompt was woken with, or a row bound to its session id.

test.description: Drives the real hook with synthetic Stop payloads: blocks the run woken for a task, never twice for the same item, never under stop_hook_active, leaves an unrelated headless worker and any other session in the seat untouched, hands the session that ASKED its answer and nobody else in that seat, consumes it by showing it, and allows on no-mail / non-agent cwd / kill switches / malformed input. Every switch is checked against a transcript proved to block without it.

subsystems.notes: Marker dir: {JSTACK_REVIEW_STATE}/inbox-guarded/<session_id>, holding the message ids already blocked on.

systems.notes: Self-contained python3 stdlib. Store is the `messages` table in {timeline_dir}/timeline.db — bin/msg is its only sanctioned writer, same law log_event holds for `entries`; the one crossing is at close, where an answered task writes one timeline entry per seat. An UPDATE is addressed to a seat and rides SessionStart injection. A TASK is addressed to a session: origin_session is the far end, bound_session is NULL until the spawned session claims it (naming one before it boots is a guess, in the column the whole anti-ambush rule reads), wake_job is the one-shot booked to carry it. A reply goes back to origin_session by whichever of two racing paths gets there first — that session's next Stop, or a fork-resume wake booked against the workspace it started in — so no liveness guess is needed anywhere. A task is NEVER typed into a session already running: a rung that did that (mail.deliver_live) was removed 2026-08-27 because mail addresses a seat and a seat is a chat dir, so every session it could resolve was a conversation, and it picked the most recently active one, which is by construction the one a person is typing in. A stop stays safe — it is the harness's own continuation channel and touches no composer. The scheduler rung is optional; with no `mail` config the inbox still files, injects and enforces, but a task cannot be delivered. Hosts adding entrances (share-sheet drops, dashboard forms) shell out to bin/msg rather than writing the table.

systems.name: Repo Seats
systems.description: Gives a seat to a session whose cwd is a repo instead of a workspace directory — the shape an IDE forces, since editors fix cwd to the checked-out repo. repo_seat.py resolves the directory to the agent that owns it via the agent registry's `repos` (the same map /jstack:day-audit dispatches on), and to that agent's own registered `workspace` read back as a seat, so IDE work joins the agent's one running memory instead of starting cold and ending silent. Resolution: git toplevel → basename → remote.origin.url (carries worktrees) → longest normalized prefix (carries `<Repo>-issue-42`), names normalized so Acme_iOS == Acme-iOS == git@github.com:org/Acme_iOS.git. A real seat directory always wins over the registry; `"active": false` entries never claim. Consulted by the SessionStart injection hook and the session-end engine only after normal {agent_root}-relative resolution comes up empty, so a host with no registry is unaffected. bin/ide-bridge wires the IDE half over ACP: an editor will run any Agent Client Protocol agent as a subprocess with the open project as its working directory, which is both halves at once — our own CLI, and the cwd the seat resolves from. bin/acp-agent is that subprocess; registration is one manual step in the IDE's own UI (Xcode: Settings > Intelligence > Add an Agent... > Add an ACP Agent, Executable = bin/acp-agent, everything else empty) because the IDE stores it with no documented defaults key, and one registration covers every repo. acp-agent fixes the two things that would otherwise leave the session a stranger: @zed-industries/claude-code-acp bundles its own CLI inside the Agent SDK which loads no plugins (so no hooks, no seat, no timeline, and the SDK's model rather than the host's), answered by pointing CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE at the installed CLI; and an IDE launches subprocesses login-less, with PATH down to /usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin and often no USER, which hides node/claude/the adapter and alone makes the keychain read fail — both rebuilt before anything resolves, and the same bare PATH is why acp-agent carries `from __future__ import annotations` (system python3 is 3.9). CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is deliberately left unset so the CLI reads the login keychain: the IDE session is signed in because the terminal is, with no second sign-in and no download. ide-bridge also links each owned repo's auto-memory to its agent's, refusing to overwrite a repo that already holds memories of its own. The earlier approach — pointing the IDE's built-in agent at the host config directory via IDEChatOverrideAgenticHomeDirectory — is retired as unworkable and flagged by status if still set: setting CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at all (any path, the host's own included) moves Claude Code off the login keychain onto a credentials file, and the built-in agent authenticates through the IDE's own sign-in (com.apple.dt.Xcode.ClaudeAgent.*, passed to the CLI as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN) which no config directory satisfies. A repo-seated session is also handed its role files as a <jstack-identity> block — the shared protocol, the agent's role file and the seat's — because walk-up climbs ancestors and the workspace is a sibling of the checkout, so a repo session would otherwise arrive with no identity at all; a session already in the workspace gets nothing extra (inject_identity: false disables it).

test.description: Hermetic live test — temp agents tree, temp registry, real git checkouts, temp timeline. Each resolution rule (registry name, subdirectory of a checkout, _/- spelling, git origin, <Repo>-issue-42 prefix), unowned repo → exit 3, inactive entry never claims, seat derived from the entry's workspace rather than a fixed 'chat', a real seat directory beating the registry, end-to-end SessionStart injection in an owned repo, and no-registry → silent unchanged behavior.

systems.notes: Additive by construction: every caller falls back to it only after the normal {agent_root}-relative resolution returns nothing, and it returns nothing itself without a readable registry. Registry default {agent_root}/agents.json, override with agent_registry (or JSTACK_AGENT_REGISTRY). ide-bridge scans repo_root (default parent of agent_root) and reports the repos no entry owns — those open in the IDE as no agent until a line is added to some entry's `repos`. The ACP agent is registered in the IDE's UI, not via defaults — ide-bridge status detects it by looking for acp-agent's path in the Xcode domain. Requires `npm install -g @zed-industries/claude-code-acp`; overrides for both halves are JSTACK_CLAUDE_EXECUTABLE / JSTACK_ACP_ADAPTER in the environment or claude_executable / acp_adapter in the review config. Liveness: injection is live-session-only and an IDE chain holds no tty anywhere, so session-start-inject counts an IDE ancestor as live (JSTACK_IDE_ANCESTORS, default Xcode) — without that the seat resolves and nothing is injected. bin/pict resolves repo seats too, so it previews exactly what an IDE session in a repo would receive.

systems.name: Commit identity guard
systems.description: Pre-commit hook for the jStack checkout itself: this repo is public, and a commit made under the wrong local git identity once put a private employer email into its history. The hook refuses any commit whose author or committer email is off an explicit allowlist (the org agent account, the owner's GitHub noreply, and the historical agent@local), and the refusal message states the `git config user.email` fix. Default-deny: a new identity is added to the allowlist in the hook file, never forced past it. .git/hooks is untracked, so the versioned copy lives at githooks/pre-commit and a clone restores it with `ln -s ../../plugins/jstack/githooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit` — the same symlink pattern as the pre-push gate.

test.description: Hermetic fixture repo with the hook installed: an off-list author email is blocked with the fix in the message, an off-list committer is blocked even under a good author, and an on-list identity commits normally.

systems.name: Org-identity scrub gate
systems.description: The plugin was built inside one private operation before it shipped public, and its release history is squashed: whatever identity sits in the tree at a cut is permanent. This gate scans every git-tracked file (contents and paths) for the terms of that operation — its people, its principal's persona, its closed-source siblings, its machine paths — and fails naming file, line and term. One extensible term list; a per-(file, term) allowlist where each load-bearing wire literal (the shipped default board name, the commit-identity allowlist's own addresses) carries its reason; a stale allowlist entry fails too, so an exemption outlives its carrier by zero releases. Lowercase `boss`/`@boss` is deliberately off the list: the refused address and the `--from boss` convention are shipped behavior, only the capitalized persona is banned.

test.description: Runs the scan itself against the real tree: exit 0 with the scanned-file count when no org term appears outside the reasoned allowlist, exit 1 naming every file:line and term when one does.

systems.name: Version-bump gate
systems.description: A plugin is installed BY VERSION: the CLI caches the tree under <market>/<plugin>/<version>/ and `plugin update` compares numbers, never contents. So a runtime file changed on main without a bump is invisible — every installed machine keeps running the cached copy while `update` answers "already at the latest version", and nothing anywhere reports the drift. Five commits shipped that way behind an unbumped 0.59.0. This gate finds the commit that set the version now on disk (keyed on the version VALUE, so editing the manifest's description does not read as a release), then fails if anything under plugins/jstack outside tests/ moved since — naming each commit. tests/ is excluded because nothing an installed copy runs comes from there. It reads history, so where there is none to read — a shallow clone, an unpacked tarball — it says SKIP and stands down rather than reporting a green it cannot see.

test.description: Runs the gate itself against the real tree: exit 0 naming the bump commit when the version covers every shipped change (or when the bump is staged but not yet committed), exit 1 listing every shipped commit the current version does not cover, with the two manifests to bump.

systems.notes: A bump makes new source installable; it does not hot-reload an already-running CLI. Acceptance of a native/zero-turn Codex command requires all three steps: bump the cache key, `codex plugin add jstack@jstack`, then invoke it from a brand-new Codex process under the same hook-trust mode production uses and inspect that rollout. On a host whose managed launcher supplies `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, the probe must supply it too; a bare `codex exec` with no persisted trust tests the trust gate, not the command hook. A checkout fixture or a session opened on the prior cache cannot prove the installed environment intercepted before inference.

systems.name: Structure manifest
systems.description: The repo is a closed set at both of its roots — the repo top and the plugin top — declared entry-by-entry with reasons in structure.json, the same treatment a host's home root gets. New addition = manifest edit with a reason in the same commit; a tracked entry the manifest does not name blocks the push (the gate's layer 2 runs every tests/*.sh), and a manifest entry with nothing tracked behind it is a stale claim that blocks the same way. The listing is derived from git-tracked files — what a clone gets — never a raw directory read, because the checkout is shared and untracked work-in-progress is not the repo's shape. The manifest's _doc also carries the boundary law this structure exists to defend: the plugin is mechanisms that run on a stranger's machine, parameterized only by userConfig and JSTACK_* env; the repo above it is distribution and products (catalogs, installer, app, host package); anything host-specific lives in that host's own repo on top of the plugin, never inside it.

test.description: Against the real tree: derives both root listings from git ls-files, compares each to structure.json in both directions — unmanaged tracked entries fail naming each with the fix (declare with a reason, same commit), stale manifest entries fail naming what nothing tracks, and an unreadable manifest or unlistable tree is a failure, never a pass.

systems.name: Seat Pad Redirect
systems.description: SessionStart replaces the client's private scratchpad with a symlink to the seat's own `pad`, so everything a session writes for the user lands in the one folder the seat already shares with them instead of a per-session temp directory nobody opens. An existing scratchpad's contents are moved across rather than stranded, and a collision keeps the pad's copy and renames the incoming one by session id. Resolution is the deepest enclosing seat, so a checkout parked inside a pad belongs to the seat above it.

test.description: Runs the real hook on both the override path and the derived default: asserts the symlink lands, that a pre-written file is rescued, that a collision renames the incoming copy, that the deepest seat wins, and that no session id, an unwritable target and garbage stdin all exit without inventing a pad.

systems.name: Compaction Carry
systems.description: PreCompact writes the checklist the summarizer must honour: uncommitted work by absolute path, the task in the user's own framing, what was ruled out and why, verification actually run, wakes booked and messages sent, and anything muted owed a restoration. Its stdout REPLACES whatever the user typed after `/compact`, so the user's own instructions are echoed first and marked as outranking the checklist, and the whole note stays short enough to read in a terminal because it is printed there too.

test.description: Pipes real PreCompact JSON through the hook: every heading present by name, the length bounds held, the user's instructions carried verbatim and positioned ahead of the checklist, no dangling header when they are absent, and the checklist still printed on empty or malformed stdin.

systems.name: Compact Delivery
systems.description: Stop hook that types `/compact` into a session that parked at the seam, waits for the boundary to land, and hands the session back its own work. It is the PRIMARY delivery path and the only one that serves a busy session: the outside sweep only ever looks at a session that has already gone QUIET, so a session that parks at a seam and keeps working is invisible to it and this hook is all it has. The engine is resolved by address, not by name — PATH first because an install outranks a guess, then the locations install.sh writes — because the name resolves through one symlink that `install.sh --uninstall` removes and nothing re-creates, and a hook that could only see the name exited 0 on every Stop for hours while the host sat installed and working. `--which` reports the resolved engine without delivering, so a health probe grades the real thing rather than re-deriving the search.

test.description: Runs the real hook against fake hosts planted in each install location: PATH outranks both fallbacks, a deleted ~/.local/bin symlink still reaches the checkout venv and still DELIVERS rather than exiting quiet, `--which` answers under the skip switch and never runs the engine, and a machine with no host at all stays silent and green while `--which` alone fails loudly — so an opt-out is never mistaken for an outage.

systems.name: Codex Compaction Carry
systems.description: Codex compacts server-side: the window is rebuilt from the user's own messages plus the developer prompts, and every assistant message and every tool result in it is dropped. Neither compaction hook on that client carries `additionalContext`, so there is no summarizer to steer — this reads the residue back off the rollout, which compaction does not touch, and injects it at EVERY boundary because an injected developer message does not survive the next one. Only what a session cannot reconstruct: the commands it ran and its own last words, with the budget going to what cannot be re-run.

test.description: Pipes real SessionStart JSON through the hook against synthetic rollouts: both tool-call shapes read, the user's own message not repeated, a poll loop carried once, a booked wake outranking eighty re-runnable lines, a torn line survived, startup silent, and a Claude transcript left to Claude.

systems.name: Memory Index Ceiling
systems.description: PreToolUse caps the auto-memory index at a readable length, because an index that grows without bound is loaded into every session of that project and stops being an index. A Write is judged on the content in the payload; an Edit or MultiEdit is judged on the file as it stands on disk. The denial names the current count and the layers that own durable rules instead, so the answer to a full index is moving a line, not deleting one.

test.description: Pipes real PreToolUse JSON through the hook: an over-ceiling Write denied with a reason naming the count and the other layers, exactly at the ceiling allowed, Edit and MultiEdit judged on disk, four non-index paths untouched, and an empty or malformed payload allowed through.

systems.name: Attention Marker
systems.description: Raises the waiting dot when a session is blocked on a person and lowers it the moment anything resolves, so a remote board can tell a session that needs an answer from one that is simply thinking. Only a real dialog counts — the two dialog tools and a permission notification — while an idle notification does not. The marker lands in the state directory the Hub's embed marker DECLARES, not one the hook guesses, which is what makes it work on a machine whose Hub is mounted into another server; the same file also carries the turn clock, opened on a prompt and closed at the seam.

test.description: Pipes real hook JSON through the hook and reads the marker off disk: the two dialog tools and a permission notification raise it, an idle notification does not, every resolution lowers it, the marker lands where a synthetic embed marker declares, an environment override outranks that declaration, and a session id that is a path writes nothing outside.

systems.name: Host Loader
systems.description: The one place a hook finds the host package. parents[3] of a hook is the repo only in a checkout; Claude Code and Codex run an installed plugin from their plugin cache, where that path holds nothing, so every host-importing hook exited 0 having done nothing on every installed machine while the suites, run from a checkout, passed. _host.py resolves the checkout beside the plugin or through the directory marketplace it was installed from, records a failed load in one line jstack-doctor's host check reads, and re-execs once under the checkout venv when the PATH python is below the host's floor, stdin handed over.

test.description: Copies the plugin into a cache layout under a redirected HOME and proves resolution through known_marketplaces.json and Codex config.toml, refusal of a directory with no host package, the one-line failure receipt and its removal on success, that context-ceiling run from the cache copy speaks only once a marketplace names a checkout, and that a below-floor interpreter re-execs exactly once.

systems.name: Context Ceiling
systems.description: Tells a session it has got heavy while ending the turn is still cheap, on the load meter's measured cuts rather than the client's configured window — a running session resolves that window once at startup and never re-reads it. Fires once per band on the CROSSING, heaviest band first so a double jump takes the louder, and names the session's own measured floor and what a boundary would free rather than a generic figure. No band at any size prescribes a handoff, because handing off lands below a compaction of the same session and pays for it with the whole live thread.

test.description: Builds both transcript dialects in-file and pipes real hook JSON through: each cut fires on its crossing only, already-in-band and falling are silent, one message written three times is still one reading, the floor and freed figures are named, the Codex note says server-side and the Claude note does not, and an unreadable transcript stays silent rather than fatal.

systems.name: Turn Budget
systems.description: Caps how long an UNATTENDED run may keep taking turns, because the failure mode of a session nobody is watching is not a wrong answer but an endless one. A soft cut warns with the count, the share of turns that carried no tool call, and the hard cut ahead; the hard cut denies the tool and says to commit, push and book a wake rather than ask to continue.
