Only sessions with no human engaged are policed — a typed prompt, a mode row or a CLI rollout exempts a session at any count — and a missing or corrupt budget file fails open to the shipped default.

test.description: Pipes real PreToolUse JSON through the hook in both dialects: silent under the soft cut, the warning carrying the counts and the hard cut, the hard cut denying with the wake instruction, an engaged session never policed at any count, per-kind budgets honoured, and a corrupt budget file falling back to the shipped default.

systems.name: Session Environment
systems.description: How a session WORKS — deliver by distribute or by build, run the simulator journey or skip it, one agent or one per plan stage — said once per session or per agent and carried by three hooks instead of restated at the top of every sitting. Entry states what is in force, a flip between prompts emits the one line that moved, and a matching tool call repeats the directive once per session per value. Every rendered string comes from the host registry, so the four surfaces cannot word a setting four ways, and a value at its default renders NOTHING anywhere: a host where nobody has set anything injects not one word into any session.

test.description: Drives the three real hook scripts against a store and an agent tree built for the run: an untouched environment silent at all three moments, entry carrying only the moved values in one <jstack-environment> block, the cold start reaching the agent layer for a session the index has never seen and a session value still shadowing it once indexed, one delta line per flip and silence otherwise, one announcement per value across eleven matching calls, a flip re-arming it, a .swift edit firing in an otherwise-infra session, and command patterns matched on the command line. Also pins the hooks.json ordinals and checks every tool the registry triggers on is covered by a matcher.

systems.notes: Kill switch for all three hooks: JSTACK_ENV_INJECT_DISABLED=1. Announcement dedup markers sit beside the path-rule markers in /tmp/jstack-rule-cache/<session_id>/ as env-<key>-<value>.marker — keyed on the VALUE so a mid-session flip re-arms rather than being swallowed; re-announcement only after JSTACK_RULE_REINJECT_BYTES of transcript growth. env-delta.py keeps its per-session snapshot in the same dir as environment.json. hooks.json is APPEND-ONLY: Codex keys hook trust by ordinal, so a group or hook inserted above an existing one silently stops it running. env-announce.py's PreToolUse and PostToolUse groups carry matchers rather than taking every tool, because these hooks import the host (~40ms a call) and one beside every tool call of every session may not. All three hooks resolve the agent from the payload's cwd (`_env.seat_agent`), not only from the session index, so a session the indexer has not reached still hears its agent's values and their changes. The agent env routes store under the bare lowercased agent name whatever id `/agents` served (`alpha-chat` -> `alpha`), the one key every reader asks with. The live journey is verify/scenarios/hub/work-env.sh (`verify/run.sh run hub/work-env`): a Hub installed from the ref under test, values drawn per run and POSTed to the session and agent routes, and the real session made to repeat the injected line — control, session layer, agent layer under the scoped id, per-key precedence, a mid-session agent flip reaching env-delta, and env-announce's value-keyed markers read back by the host as `announced`.

systems.name: Work Harness
systems.description: Plan mode becomes rows, on both engines. `permission_mode: "plan"` is on every hook payload of Claude and Codex alike and nothing read it before this; it is the whole cross-vendor seam. The row is minted at the first plan-mode prompt, the stages are parsed at approval, and each stage declares the proof that closes it — command, commit, artifact, manual or none. The writer refuses to close a stage whose declared gate has no passing proof, so "is this done" is answered by a stage id and its receipt rather than by a sentence. `none` is a real answer: the bureaucracy scales with the severity of the change instead of taxing a one-line tweak.

test.description: Drives the three real hook scripts with the real JSON stdin contract against a store built for the run. The property it protects hardest is CONTAINMENT: plan-exit.py stands in front of ExitPlanMode for every session on this machine, so every shape that must NOT block — a 0-stage plan, a 1-stage plan, a merely cosmetic complaint, a hook that threw — is pinned as hard as the one shape that must. Also pins the planning row minted once per session on both engines, the authored title and plan_file reaching a row that was minted from a prompt, the Codex exit staying honest about what it does not have, native tasks mirrored from both engines, the hooks.json ordinals as append-only, and the Codex matchers dropping the groups Codex could never fire.

systems.notes: Kill switch for the gate: JSTACK_PLAN_GATE_DISABLED=1. plan-exit.py blocks only a plan that parses to >=2 stages AND holds a stage the writer would refuse, and it fails OPEN on its own exception — a traceback out of a PreToolUse hook reads as a broken tool, not a broken plan. The refusal carries the format contract inline because plan mode does not author through Edit, so the path-scoped rule in rules-stage/execution-gates.md never injected and the model being blocked has never seen it. hooks.json is APPEND-ONLY: Codex keys hook trust by ordinal. plan-mode-watch.py reads its marker and returns BEFORE importing the host, which is what keeps a turn that is not in plan mode at +14ms rather than +58ms. The live journey is verify/scenarios/plugin/plan-gate.sh (`verify/run.sh run plugin/plan-gate`): a real authed guest with the Hub installed from the ref under test (JSTACK_VERIFY_REF, default dev — a default-branch install carries no harness), a real `claude --permission-mode plan` session authoring verify/fixtures/plan-demo's plan, both Verify: gates refused on the untouched project, a hand-filed proof retired by a re-approval that tightens stage 2, the session's own edits turning each gate green, and each plan hook proved by its side effect (plan-mode.json, stage rows, stage_tasks rows plus the stage id stamped into ~/.claude/tasks/<sid>/, env markers) and read back through /sessions/{sid}/work and /plans/{id} — every surface tests/plan-hooks.sh cannot reach, because nothing in it spawns an engine. `plan verify` with no --cwd runs in the plan's `repo`, so a relative Verify: line grades the tree the plan was authored in.
